title: Heat through a thin wall between two held plates: a zero-thickness sheet of conductance 0.05 between fluid layers of conductivity 0.05, 1 and 0 at the plates
source: Series thermal resistances: steady one-dimensional conduction through the fluid layers and the sheet's resistance 1/G, q = ΔT/(L/k_f + 1/G), each side's temperature the held plate's less q times its layer's resistance (F. P. Incropera, D. P. DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, §3.1, the composite wall)

quantities.quantity: heat flux into the sheet from the hot side, ΔT/(L/k_f + 1/G)
quantities.reason: the steady discrete profile is the exact series solution (a linear field either side of the sheet), reached to round-off after five diffusion times L²/α

quantities.quantity: the sheet's hot-side temperature, T_hot − q (L/2)/k_f
quantities.reason: the steady discrete profile is the exact series solution (a linear field either side of the sheet), reached to round-off after five diffusion times L²/α

quantities.quantity: the sheet's cold-side temperature, T_cold + q (L/2)/k_f
quantities.reason: the steady discrete profile is the exact series solution (a linear field either side of the sheet), reached to round-off after five diffusion times L²/α
